vignette: Akua had always been an active and engaged member of her community, but that changed on a fateful night two years ago when she was involved in a life-threatening motor vehicle collision. The accident left her with physical scars, but it was the emotional impact that proved more debilitating. As a policy analyst, Akua spent most of her days reviewing data and attending meetings, but even these mundane tasks had become daunting challenges. The slightest whiff of alcohol or burnt smell would instantly transport Akua back to the night of the accident. She remembered the sound of screeching tires, the crunching metal, and the feeling of weightlessness as her car spun out of control. But it was the sensation of heat on her skin that seemed to trigger the most visceral response - a specific temperature that brought back the memory of flames licking at the wreckage. These sensory cues would send Akua's mind racing, putting her immediately on high alert for potential threats. She would become hypervigilant, scanning her surroundings for any signs of danger, and even sudden movements by others would make her jump. As she navigated this new reality, Akua found herself increasingly consumed by negative emotions - fear, anger, guilt, and shame all swirling together in a toxic stew. These feelings would often culminate in flashbacks, where she would suddenly feel as though the accident was happening all over again. Her mind would become foggy, and she would be back behind the wheel, careening out of control through the darkness. It was during these episodes that Akua's memories of the event would resurface with crystalline clarity - some moments etched in her mind like they had happened yesterday. However, there were also moments when Akua would push the memory away before she could fully recall it. She knew this wasn't healthy, but she couldn't bear to relive that night again and again. The blocked memories only seemed to intensify her fear of sudden movements or loud noises, creating a self-reinforcing cycle that was becoming increasingly difficult to break. As time went on, Akua's avoidance behaviors became more pronounced. She stopped attending social gatherings, fearful of encountering triggers that might send her spiraling back into the past. Her work began to suffer as well - she would become easily distracted and withdrawn during meetings, unable to focus on anything except the threat lurking just beneath the surface. Despite her best efforts, Akua couldn't shake the feeling that danger was always just around the corner, waiting to pounce. This pervasive sense of threat had become a constant companion, one that only seemed to intensify as the memories of the accident lingered in her mind like an open wound. It was this desperate desire for relief from the pain and fear that finally brought Akua to seek help - she knew she couldn't keep living like this, trapped in a never-ending cycle of terror and avoidance. In her darkest moments, Akua wondered if she would ever be able to break free from the grip of the accident. Would she always be haunted by the memories of that terrible night? The uncertainty was almost too much to bear, but with each passing day, she knew she had to keep trying - for herself, and for the life she once knew.
